propositions: The gate matches field names globally via a set of bare terminal names rather than resolving reads to their owning dataclass, allowing inert fields with commonly-reused names (e.g. 'enabled', 'readonly') to pass if any unrelated config reads the same-named attribute.

A synthetic inert field (e.g. CodeHealthConfig.enabled with zero reads) passes the unfixed gate because UiConfig.enabled is read elsewhere, proving the false-negative mechanism: same-named attributes on unrelated objects satisfy the gate.

The fix must resolve each read's receiver expression to its declaring schema class through six patterns (section attributes, annotations, alias assignments, return types, conditionals, and cross-module call-site propagation) so a field is satisfied only by reads of its own class.

Four live fields are newly flagged by the corrected gate and must each receive a factual `# read-via:` marker naming their actual reader (not a decoy unrelated field with the same name), per the operator ruling: McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, and JiraConfig.allow_insecure.

Both test files (test_check_config_reads.py and test_check_config_reads_heldout.py) must be migrated from the old global-name contract to the owner-resolution contract, with test_unrelated_same_named_attribute_keeps_the_gate_quiet inverted to expect a firing.
A RED-first test must prove the old gate passes an inert field reusing a common name while the fixed gate fails it, by running both versions against a synthetic schema snapshot.
